"body": "## What this PR does, in one sentence

The cache of remote resources now has one directory for each kind of resource, `git/` and `oci/`, and a Git checkout is placed in its directory only once it is complete.

## Context

Compose keeps what it fetches for a remote Compose file in a cache, one directory for each commit or digest. The two loaders do not do it the same way: extracted OCI artifacts sit at the root of the cache, and Git checkouts sit there too, next to them.

The Git loader also checks a commit out directly into its directory, and takes the directory for a valid entry as soon as it exists. A run interrupted during the fetch or the checkout (Ctrl-C, a dropped connection, a killed process) leaves a partial directory, and every later run uses it, with no sign that something is missing.

## What the PR brings

- A Git checkout is made in a directory of its own and renamed to the one of its commit once complete, so the directory of a commit is never a partial checkout. Runs which check out the same commit together end with one entry, and none of them fails because another was first. This is the same approach the OCI loader already has for its entries.
- Checkouts live in `<cache>/git/<sha>` and extracted OCI artifacts in `<cache>/oci/<digest>`, so the cache has the same structure for both.

Not changed: how a reference is resolved to a commit or a digest, what is checked out or extracted, the offline behavior, and the files that are loaded.

One consequence: what earlier releases left at the root of the cache is no longer looked for, so a remote resource is fetched again the first time it is used after the upgrade. The old directories are not removed.
